ann_29.text: This part acts on only 15 of 242 training patients (6%), all of them patients with a fixed defect on the thallium scan; 9 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 57-year-old man with a fixed thallium defect, 1 vessel coloured, a flat ST segment, 1.5 mm of ST depression and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG), it lowers the predicted risk from about 99% to about 81% (the model has little data on this; on the training data only).
Through it, a fixed defect lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 16% to about 1% (15 patients; the model has little data on this; on the training data only).

Across the whole model, a fixed defect lowers the predicted risk if fasting blood sugar is 120 mg/dL or less (from about 16% to about 2%), but the other way if it is above 120 mg/dL (from about 4% to about 9%). The model has little data on this: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).
For the typical patient this part acts on, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL raises the predicted risk from about 81% to about 99% through it (on the training data only).

ann_30.text: This part acts on 42 of 242 training patients (17%), all of them patients with atypical angina; 8 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 52-year-old man with atypical angina, no ST depression and a maximum heart rate of 164 beats per minute), it slightly lowers the predicted risk, from about 6% to about 5% (on the training data only).
Through it, atypical angina rather than any other chest pain type slightly lowers a typical patient's predicted risk, from about 16% to about 15% (on the training data only).

ann_31.text: Through this part, a higher maximum heart rate (118 to 175 beats per minute) lowers a typical patient's predicted risk only slightly, from about 17% to about 15%, and only once it rises above about 134 beats per minute (on the training data only).

An ST-T wave abnormality on the resting ECG changes the predicted risk and the heart-rate effect only slightly here (2 patients; the model has little data on this; on the training data only); without that abnormality the fall with heart rate is slow at first, then faster.

ann_32.text: For a typical patient, the model clearly gives a lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina (about 1%), non-anginal chest pain (about 2%) or atypical angina (about 9%) than with no chest pain symptoms (about 16%).

Each extra vessel coloured adds about the same: going from 0 to 2 vessels raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 16% to about 96%, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher, and a flat rather than upsloping ST segment at peak exercise raises it to about 72% (on the training data only).

Higher cholesterol, more ST depression on exercise and higher resting blood pressure raise it steadily: from about 9% at 193 mg/dL to about 34% at 308 mg/dL, from about 12% at 0 mm to about 33% at 2.8 mm, and from about 9% at 110 mm Hg to about 30% at 155 mm Hg (on the training data only).
A reversible defect or the undefined code 4 on the thallium scan raises it to about 37%, and chest pain brought on by exercise to about 29% (on the training data only).
Being a woman lowers it to about 1%, and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 4% (on the training data only).
A higher maximum heart rate lowers it slowly at first, then faster, from about 22% at 118 to about 13% at 175 beats per minute (on the training data only).
A downsloping ST segment raises it to about 23% (17 patients; the model has little data on this; on the training data only).

Smaller effects, each changing the predicted risk only slightly (on the training data only): older age raises it steadily, from about 14% at 42 to about 18% at 66 years, and an ST-T wave abnormality on the resting ECG raises it a little (2 patients, so the model has little data on this).

ann_29.original: Fixed-thallium-defect correction gate. 2065 = ReLU(0.795*thal:6 - 0.885*fbs:1 - 0.719) on z-scored one-hots is a discrete indicator: 0 unless thal:6=1 (fixed defect), 2.727 if additionally fasting blood sugar is normal, 0.148 if fbs>120. It enters the logit with weight -1.117 (-3.05) and, via identity_707, adds 2.178*2065 to the thalach gate 707 (a further ~-0.52 through 3677). Its role is to cancel the linear core's over-prediction of disease for thal:6 patients with normal FBS (the linear core gives them +0.60 through the thal:3 edge and other terms). EVIDENCE: TRAIN n=242: 2065 is exactly 0 for all thal:6=0 patients (227/242). thal:6=1 & fbs:1=0 (n=10): 2065=2.727; thal:6=1 & fbs:1=1 (n=5): 2065=0.148. Active 6.2%. Sensitivity (mean |grad|): fbs:1 0.055, thal:6 0.049. Readout: direct -1.117*2065 => logit -3.05 for fixed-defect/normal-FBS patients; via identity_707 -> 707 -> 3677 a further ~-0.52. Mean-ablating 2065 lowers train AUC 0.9424 -> 0.9363 and acc 0.884 -> 0.872. On the 10 thal:6&normal-FBS patients (disease rate 0.5) the linear core alone gives mean logit +3.78 (9/10 predicted diseased; thal:6 patients get +0.60 from the negative thal:3 edge); with the gate the mean logit is +0.25 and all 10 are classified correctly. Thus it is a learned correction for a 10-patient subgroup the linear core over-calls (likely partly fitted to train noise).
ann_29.proposed: A part that acts only on the 15 patients with a fixed thallium defect; through it, a fixed defect lowers the predicted risk when fasting blood sugar is 120 mg/dL or less.

ann_30.original: Atypical-angina indicator. 3497 = ReLU(0.984*cp:2 - 1.206) is 0 for every chest-pain type except cp=2 (atypical angina), where it is 0.941; i.e. it is exactly an affine re-coding of the cp:2 one-hot. Read out with weight -0.120, it lowers the logit by 0.113 for atypical-angina patients (disease rate 0.19 on train vs 0.50 otherwise). Functionally near-inert (ablation changes AUC by 0.0002). EVIDENCE: TRAIN n=242: 3497 takes exactly two values: 0 for the 200 non-cp:2 patients, 0.941 for the 42 atypical-angina (cp:2) patients (disease rate 0.19 vs 0.50 for others). Sensitivity mean |grad| 0.171. Logit contribution -0.120*0.941 = -0.113 for cp:2 patients. Mean-ablating 3497: AUC 0.9424 -> 0.9422, max |dlogit| 0.093. Near-inert: an affine function of cp:2 (no direct cp:2 -> output edge exists, so this node is the network's only use of cp:2).
ann_30.proposed: A part that acts only on patients with atypical angina and lowers their predicted risk slightly.

ann_31.original: Max-heart-rate relay with a floor. 707 = ReLU(0.944*thalach - 0.429*restecg:1 + identity_707 + 0.657), where identity_707 = 2.178*thal6_fixed_defect_gate; 3677 = 0.983*707 + 0.4385 (its ReLU never binds on train). Read out with weight -0.089 it adds a small extra protective effect of high maximum heart rate (beyond the direct thalach edge -0.196), clipped to zero for low-thalach patients (bottom ~22%), plus a small extra protective shift for fixed-defect patients. Small effect (logit SD 0.11). EVIDENCE: TRAIN n=242: 3677 is active for 100% of samples (min 0.4385), so the outer ReLU is the identity and 3677 = 0.983*707 + 0.4385. 707 is zero for 21.5% of patients (22.5% of thal:6=0 patients, i.e. thalach below ~-0.70 SD when identity_707=0 and restecg:1 normal; only 1/15 thal:6 patients, whose +5.94 from identity_707 holds the gate open). restecg:1 occurs in only 2 train patients. Sensitivity mean |grad|: identity_707 0.77, thalach 0.73, restecg:1 0.33. Readout weight -0.089 into the logit: contribution range [-0.77, -0.04], SD 0.107. Mean-ablating 3677: AUC 0.9424 -> 0.9414; replacing ReLU(707) by its pre-activation: AUC 0.9423, max |dlogit| 0.48.
ann_31.proposed: A higher maximum heart rate, above about 134 beats per minute, lowers the predicted risk slightly through this part.

summary.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results, predicted risk about 16%), the model clearly gives a much lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina (about 1%), non-anginal chest pain (about 2%) or atypical angina (about 9%).

Each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same to the predicted risk: going from 0 to 2 vessels raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 16% to about 96%, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher; a flat rather than upsloping ST segment at peak exercise raises it to about 72% (on the training data only).

A fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers the predicted risk if fasting blood sugar is 120 mg/dL or less, but the other way if it is above 120 mg/dL: for a typical patient from about 16% to about 2% in the first case, and from about 4% to about 9% in the second. The model has little data on this: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).
Being a woman lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 16% to about 1%, and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL lowers it to about 4% (on the training data only).
Older age raises it steadily but only slightly, from about 14% at 42 to about 18% at 66 years (on the training data only).
